batch8_regression_analysis.leading_hypothesis: The small batch is launch/dispatch/conversion-bound: BF16 Conv/MatMul work is too small to amortize fixed scheduling while BatchNorm, LIF/surrogate, reductions, optimizer work, and BF16-to-FP32 island boundaries remain numerous.
batch8_regression_analysis.observed_latency: BF16 was 26.3% slower than FP32 at batch 8.
batch8_regression_analysis.observed_memory: BF16 reduced peak allocated HBM by 14.9% and peak reserved HBM by 16.1%.
secondary_hypotheses: Ascend physical-format conversion or temporary materialization contributes a larger fraction at batch 8.
The package-managed autocast policy uses cache_enabled=false and may add fixed dispatch or weight-conversion cost.
FP32 master parameters, gradients, optimizer state, and sensitive-state islands limit the fraction accelerated by BF16.
batch8_regression_analysis.supporting_observation: Batch-8 fixed-shape evaluation NPUGraph reached 2.421x versus eager, consistent with launch overhead being important, but evaluation graph evidence does not prove the training root cause.

bf16_vs_fp32_training_performance.protocol: five alternating fresh-process pairs; three warmups and ten synchronized measured optimizer steps per process
bf16_vs_fp32_training_performance.shape_dependence: At batch 8 the same BF16 policy was 26.3% slower than FP32 while reducing allocated HBM by 14.9%; performance claims are therefore restricted to the frozen batch-64 shape.

claim_boundary: Qualified on the stated stack: BF16 mixed eager training feasibility and three-seed 20-step stability at T=4, B=64, 224x224, D=384, six heads, four blocks; a bounded 200-update fixed-batch optimization canary; and exact fixed-shape evaluation NPUGraph replay at B=8 and B=64. Only the frozen B=64 eager training benchmark showed a BF16 latency and HBM benefit. This does not establish dataset convergence, generalization, arbitrary Spikformer variants, training NPUGraph, a custom native Spikformer operator, FP8, or universal architecture-family acceleration.
follow_up_work: Run matched BF16/FP32 Ascend stage profiles at batches 8 and 64 and report Conv/MatMul, BatchNorm, LIF/surrogate forward/backward, Cast, TransData/format conversion, reductions, optimizer step, kernel count, average kernel duration, idle gaps, AI Core utilization, and HBM bandwidth.
Separate model-only forward, forward plus backward, and full optimizer-step timing; count and time BF16-to-FP32 island boundaries without changing public semantics.
Profile batches 8, 16, 32, and 64 with the existing balanced five-fresh-process protocol to locate the BF16 crossover point and keep claims bucket-specific.
Evaluate autocast weight caching only after numerical, state, import-side-effect, and concurrency behavior are independently qualified.
Consider an exact Sigmoid-surrogate BF16-public/FP32-state multi-step LIF scan only if profiling proves launch-bound recurrence and isolated-hotspot, block, and complete-model gates pass.
Keep Spikformer training NPUGraph unsupported until the saved-tensor second-backward capture failure is understood without weakening poison/no-eager-replay semantics.
Run real-dataset multi-seed convergence/generalization only after execution profiling and route identity are stable; report it separately from optimization-health and performance evidence.

batch64.claim: Correct fixed-shape evaluation graph capability only; not an acceleration claim.
batch64.performance_gate: failed; graph replay was about 5.0% slower than eager

batch8.boundary: Useful secondary bucket, not the frozen representative batch.

training.batch8_probe: capture failed after launch with a second-backward saved-tensor error
training.failure_semantics: runner poisoned; no eager replay after launch

three_seed_twenty_step.interpretation: Numerical and optimizer-state stability on random batches; not a dataset convergence or accuracy result.

two_hundred_update_canary.interpretation: Optimization-health canary only; memorization of one fixed synthetic batch is not generalization evidence.
